note: The Fair Credit Reporting Act bars a consumer report from carrying an adverse item that antedates it by more than seven years (15 U.S.C. 1681c(a)(5)); Experian, one of the three national bureaus, says late payments are reported once at least 30 days past the due date and stay seven years from when the account first went past due.

sources.title: 15 U.S. Code § 1681c, Requirements relating to information contained in consumer reports (Legal Information Institute)
sources.said: (5) Any other adverse item of information, other than records of convictions of crimes which antedates the report by more than seven years.

sources.title: Experian, When Do Late Payments Get Reported?
sources.said: Late payments are reported to the credit bureaus once you’re at least 30 days past your bill’s due date. ... Late payments can stay on your credit report for seven years from when the account first went past due.
